q: Steve was jealous as a kid of a Christmas present his dad got. What was it?
f: It had a beige body and white arms; turned inside out, beige arms and white body, so it looked almost identical.
ex: "Yeah, alright, yeah." He comes down, they go.. "Remember that jacket I came in wearing, yeah, with a beige body? Yeah, have another look. Have another look."
"Wait a minute, that must be a completely different jacket!"
"You must be one of the richest men in Bristol!"
"But, hold on.. you weren't carrying anything -- you didn't have a bag, or anything.." "Noo.. well.. errr.. Well, okay if you must know, it's a reversible jacket, alright?" It's the best.. the best..
But.. the only idea of a reversible jacket must be so that you think people think that you've got two jackets, that's the whole point, surely.

q: XFM S1E03 went out on Steve's birthday in November 2001. How old was he?
f: Karl couldn't believe Steve was only 27.
ex: It was- Karl, it was you that worked out the maths and worked out I was 28. Cause they've just worked out I'm 27.
Yeah I tol- I asked you, didn't I? And I said-
Yeah, because- no but what I questioned was, I said well if you're 27 today, that means last week you were 26.

q: On Radio 2's New Year's Eve special, what did Steve finally give away?
f: It went to Toby in London, whose worst Christmas present was a book about crude oil.

ex: Oh yeah. Yeah yeah yeah. Um, I should just give away this Eurythmics platinum-

-that we uh, we offered up in the first hour. Um, we were asking for the worst Christmas gifts you'd ever received and, uh, I want to give it to this guy because, I- I- well... it's, it's not like, you know, I'm sure it's fine but it's…

q: Putting on a highbrow act for the Telegraph, Ricky said "Oh, Proust! I love him". What did Steve add?
a: He wished he'd resign as Governor of France
x: He's better than the film version
He should do a guest spot on Monkey News
His books could do with more pictures
f: Next Ricky praised a famous author's new novel. Steve's verdict: "It's very long."
ex: I wish he'd resign as Governor of... France.

q: Steve read out a story about a police sergeant in Japan secretly photographing up a woman's skirt while she reported a stolen bike. How did he get caught?
a: She saw the flash go off
x: The camera made a loud click
A colleague walked in on him
f: Steve imagined him bringing the camera in "on the off chance". Ricky: "Not the secret at all!"
ex: "A policeman in Japan is facing disciplinary measures after he was caught photographing upper woman's skirt with a hidden camera while on duty. The 42 year old sergeant- who's not been named- used a digital camera to secretly snap the…

He was actually doing his proper job, he'd obviously thought to himself "I'll bring him a digital camera today on the off chance a beautiful woman comes in to report a crime or robbery. I'll have it ready, I'll have it positioned in such a…
But this is interesting. This is how he got caught. Okay? The woman became suspicious after she saw a flash go off.

q: Steve insisted he'd happily pay for a Bruce Springsteen ticket, he just couldn't get one. What price did he ideally want to pay?
f: Ricky: "I thought you were mean." Steve: "Don't be crazy. You know ideally half price."
ex: Well I’m a generous kind of guy.
I thought you were mean. But go on what were you going to say.
You don’t mind paying for a ticket – Face value I mean you don’t want to be ripped off do you.
Don’t be crazy. You know ideally half price.

And I’ve been chasing, kind of, my tail really – I’m not going, at the moment I’m not going. And I’m desperate to see the man. You know, he’s going to do a great concert; it’s his only one in London. I can’t believe that being on the…

q: Steve's war-history-loving dad once told him "Never forget, son." What did Steve reply?
f: Ricky burst out laughing. Steve explained his dad "was into the military and all that, and war history and stuff."
ex: But he said to me once, he said to me: "Never forget, son."
Yeah, and I went "I don't remember, Dad!"

q: Drunk at the Monarch in Camden, Steve asked the doorman "Any discount for Xfm DJs?" What did his mates get?
a: A pound off the five-pound entry
x: In for free, same as Steve
f: Steve got in free. His reason for trying? "Impress my mates." Ricky: "How impressive is it that Steve Merchant can get you in a place for a quid off?"
ex: There was some kind of groovy night on. I went to the door, I'd got a load of mates with me, I said umm, "Any discount for Xfm DJs?"
-I was a bit drunk. He went, "who are you?" I went "Steve Merchant, Ricky Gervais." He went "Steve Merchant? Brilliant, you can come in for free"-
Yes he did, I swear to god. And I said what about my mates? He said "it's five pounds, they can have a pound off." He said "but," and I think basically-

q: Karl said old Victorian pictures show "what a smart world that is". What did Steve point out?
a: You can't see cholera on pictures
x: Nobody ever smiled in Victorian photos
Everyone in them was sat in a sooty factory
The hats were all rented for the photo
f: Karl stood firm: "The world look nicer with more cloth."
ex: When you look back at, like Victorian times and everything, everyone wore a hat, right? They wore a tie, they wore a suit and it was a nicer looking place to look at. When you see it on pictures, you go, what a smart world that is.
Well, you can't see cholera and things on pictures, but sure.

No, but I'm just saying it's better to try and cover it up with a bit of, you know, cloth. Yeah, yeah. The world look nicer with. With more cloth. Whereas now everyone's rowing about scruffily. So. So what I'm saying is if we make the tie…

q: Why, according to Steve, do his parents always take their own tea bags when they go abroad?
a: For fear of a tea bag drought in France
x: Foreign tea bags are full of twigs
To swap with the locals for wine
f: Steve: "My parents always take tea bags wherever they're going... For fear of there being some kind of tea bag drought in France."
ex: My dad does that, my parents always take, uh, tea bags wherever they're going.
For fear of- of there being some kind of tea bag drought in France.

q: Mocking Karl's 'bombs do you a favour' theory, Steve imagined a survivor saying: "My family was killed, but look! A..."
f: Steve also wondered whether Afghanistan now had "a brand new B & Q", with locals "popping down there every Sunday."
ex: Yeah. Cause they’ve got a brand new B & Q, have they, over now?
They’re popping down there every Sunday.
Anyway. Let’s not go on about it, cause--
“My family was killed, but look! A Carpet Warehouse!”

q: When Ricky banned Karl's 'Songs of Phrase', what did Steve suggest doing with the competition prizes instead?
a: Sharing them out amongst the homeless
x: Giving them to the peace marchers
Sending them back to the record label
f: Ricky agreed: "There's troubles in the world and I'm not going to let you faff around doing nonsense like that."
ex: I’ll tell you, we’ve got the prizes--
But I’m not even going to bother giving- I’m not even going to bother. I-I think we’ll just share them out amongst, um--
Absolutely. N-no. There’s-there’s troubles in the world and I’m not going to let you faff around doing nonsense like that.

q: Karl couldn't get over Steve's excuse for missing their midweek meeting to plan new features. What was it?
a: He had to stay in and tidy up because his landlady was coming
x: He was waiting in for a washing machine delivery
He was rehearsing his Sony Awards speech
f: Ricky: "He talked about it for about the hour, when we were working." In Steve's defence, Karl only rang him "about an hour before" the meeting.
ex: Where were you in the week? I said, I said "Let's meet up. Let's, you know, come up with some new features and that." Where were you?
Karl, you phoned me about an hour before you wanted to meet. That is not what I would call-- I mean, that is arrogance right there!
That's arrogance right there! That's ego right there.
He couldn't- He couldn't get-- When I came in, he said "Where's Steve?" I said "Steve can't make it."

I had to tell him why. Steve was staying in to tidy up, because his landlady was coming. This- This, he couldn't get over. He could not get over that you couldn't make it because you had to stay in for your landlady. He's- He talked about…

q: Ricky moaned that their faces are on posters in tube stations with people laughing at them. What did Steve claim people really say about him?
f: Steve: "Well, they're not laughing at me, Rick." When Ricky asked Karl what people think of the posters, there was a long pause before Steve cut in: "I don't want to know his opinion!"
ex: We have to be on tube stations, people laughing at us.
Yeah. Well, they're not laughing at me, Rick.
They're saying there's a good-looking fella, they're just-

q: Steve wondered why popcorn became the cinema snack. What quieter food did he suggest they serve instead?
f: Ricky wasn't having it: "The slurping would drive me mad. And the spoon touching the bottom of the thing would drive me mad."
ex: But I don't know why it was that popcorn became the thing you eat in the cinema. It's like you say, you've made these films and someone's there thinking, well, we've made this great film, we've got the sound mix right. But what we need is…
Yea and do you see, have you seen the size of the bucket they go in, their popcorn?
But why not serve soup or something, or yoghurt?
Ugh the slurping would drive me mad. And the spoon touching the bottom of the thing would drive me mad.
But something where it's not going to make a noise.
Don't serve anything! There's no reason you have to go to the cinema and think "Oh God, I need to eat." Eat- plan it! You don't go and play tennis eating while- you plan it, don't you?

q: Steve said a 16-year-old taking a phone call in the cinema could only be excused if the caller was who?
a: Her business partner in Hong Kong, saying the deal's off
x: Her lawyer in New York, about her trial
A talent scout from Smash Hits
f: Steve suspected it was really "Gareth or Gavin or your boyfriend Tony". His advice: "Switch off the phone or very least, get out."
ex: But let's say instead of it being, instead of immediately thinking "Oh God" and switching it off hurriedly, they take the call in the cinema. "I'm in the cinema. Yeah. No, I'm in duh duh duh." Start having a conversation. And I was…
Switch off the phone or very least, get out.

q: What was the 'a little bit complicated' premise of Steve's feature 'A Song That I Like'?
a: Steve plays a song that he likes
x: Listeners vote on a song Steve hates
Karl picks a song and Steve rates it
Steve plays a song he's never heard
f: Steve: "let me explain, it's a little bit complicated… I play a song… that I like." He picked Patti Smith's "Gloria".
ex: It’s brilliantly, it’s rather brilliantly called “A Song That I Like.”
And in it, let me explain, it’s a little bit complicated.
What I do is, in it, I play a song…

q: Steve pictured fussy Ricky at the feeding of the multitude saying 'I'm not into the fish, JC.' What condition did Steve say Ricky would set for the bread?
a: It had to be Mighty White
x: It had to have the crusts cut off
It had to be from Greggs
f: Steve: "Unless that bread is mighty white, I'm not interested." Ricky added his fish orders: "take the head off... I can see a bit of spine."
ex: And you're there, and Jesus Christ has just fed 40,000 with some fishes and some loaves, you'd be going "I'm not into the fish, JC" and -
I'd say "take the head off, cook, really cook, take the skin off, there's, I can see a bit of spine, and while you're gutting -
Unless that bread is mighty white, I'm not interested.

q: Steve was gutted to miss a band at a pub near his parents' place in Bristol, purely because they had the least evocative name ever. What were they called?
f: Steve: "It's not sexy, it's nothing." Ricky reckoned it was up there with "Rough outline" and "Pocket fluff".
ex: Yeah, I went back to Bristol at the weekend. As you know, we all had a bit of time off and actually I was quite annoyed because I passed the pub near where my parents live and they had a band on. You know, pubs sometimes have a band on and…
Loose Change, it's. It's just, it's welcome. Rough outline. Yeah, it's just nothing.

q: Steve wanted Rockbusters scrapped. What did he say would be better in that part of the show?
f: Steve: "Might be better just have silence during that part of the show than have Rockbusters!"
ex: No I was wondering whether we should perhaps not do a quiz at all rather than do that piece of rubbish.
Might be better to have nothing. Might be better just have silence during that part of the show than have Rockbusters!
How about if I give you the clues and that and if you think "they sound rubbish we're not doing it".
Well, I guarantee they're going to sound rubbish. All right, let's make it the last Rockbuster's then, this is the last Rockbusters.

q: Steve saw a homeless man studying cable TV deals in a Dixons window. What did Steve say his first step should be?
a: Start eating his dinner off a plate
x: Get a sleeping bag with a cup holder
Buy a copy of the Radio Times
Save up for a TV aerial
f: Steve said take it "one step at a time" and then work up to "a house, a home, a wide-screen TV."
ex: We were talking about the homeless; I saw a homeless guy in the week as I was walking in Finchley Road, and he was peering in the window of one of, the, Dixon's, or something like that. Just checking out the details on one of those cable…
And then work your way up to you know, a house, a home, a wide-screen TV.

q: As a glasses wearer, what drives Steve mad when people ask to try his glasses on?
a: They always say "Oh! I can't see a thing!"
x: They always leave thumbprints on the lenses
They say "Now I look like you!"
f: Steve: "What were you expecting? X-ray vision!? No!"
ex: Tell you what frustrates me. Can I just say, as a glasses wearer, this is just a-a note to everyone out there who isn’t a glasses wearer. When people ask constantly to try on your glasses- “Can I try on your glasses?" and they try them on…
If you’re a glasses wearer, you don’t want people asking to try on your glasses.
But I think they don’t realize that--

q: When Ricky explained that flowers use phototropism and turn towards the sun, what did Steve ask him to stop doing?
f: Steve: "Can you stop using long words, Rick? Like sun." It was the right level for a debate about whether worms can think.
ex: Again, they use phototropism. They go towards the sun. They close and open.
Can you stop using long words, Rick? Like sun.

q: Steve recalled a Feng shui woman who said his office needed a £25 crystal to get the negative chi out. What happened when he refused to pay that?
a: She produced another one for a fiver
x: She offered to come back and cleanse it for free
She warned the chi would follow him home
She knocked it down to twenty quid
f: She went, "Okay, I've got one for five." Steve: "It was surprisingly convenient that she had a number of different crystals that apparently did the same job."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Philosophy · 2009
ex: The interesting thing about Feng shui is how I remember someone came into an office I was working at once, and she said, "You're going to need crystal here above the laboratory to get all the negative chi out of the system," And she said…
It was surprisingly convenient that she had a number of different crystals that apparently did the same job.

q: On the BBC World Service, a woman read Steve's personality from the coloured liquids he picked. What was her big insight?
a: He likes to communicate with people, but on a global level
x: He's a natural leader who hides his feelings
He's a creative soul stuck behind a desk
He's happiest when working through the night
f: Ricky: "You're working for the World Service." Steve: "As we spoke, we were broadcasting on the World Service."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Philosophy · 2009
ex: Yeah, there's a lot of that twaddle. There was a woman, I remember once, I used to do a radio show on the BBC World Service, and she came in and she could tell from the coloured liquids, that you chose from a big selection of coloured…
You're working for the World Service.

As we spoke, we were broadcasting on the World Service. I don't know, she just read it from the liquids. As a novice, one of the key catchphrases, if you like, of philosophy, and one that's always intrigued and confused me a little is the…

q: While Karl explained his 'problem hole' theory, what did Steve keep yelling at Ricky?
a: Shut up and let him explain!
f: Steve: "He's just expanding on his idea, why do you keep interrupting?" Ricky: "But what is his problem?"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Philosophy · 2009
ex: Shut up! Ricky, let him explain!
Now, Ricky... I'd say his problems are not even problems.
How big is his problem hole?
But his problems are all little ones. They're like-- You've got, like a load of Skittles, I've got a big Creme Egg.
Shut up! Let him speak his-- He's just expanding on his idea, why do you keep interrupting?

q: Steve claimed he was one of the people who bought Karl's book. Where does he say he keeps his copy?
x: In the glovebox of his car
f: Steve takes it off the shelf every visit for "a little read. Great fun!" Ricky: "I'm down to about four pages!"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Philosophy · 2009
ex: Listen, everyone like me, who's bought that book-
It's in my lavatory... Every time I pop in there for a s***, just take it off the shelf, have a little read. Great fun!
Yeah. I'm down to about four pages! Sometimes we have to get bog roll. But listen! That is a fun book to wipe your arse with!
Yeah! It's a great book to wipe your arse with!

q: What does Steve do to avoid charity collectors with clipboards on the street?
a: Gets his mobile out and pretends to have a conversation
x: Pretends he's lost and asks them for directions
f: Karl admitted "Yeah I've done that one," and Steve groaned about "the number of fake conversations I've had walking past them now."
ex: This is terrible thing to say, but when I see those people approaching now with the clipboards on the street, I always get my mobile phone out and pretend to have a conversation.
The number of fake conversations I've had walking past them now.

q: If Steve were homeless, where did he say he'd hang around to make a fortune in summer?
x: In the queue for the London Eye
On the steps of St Paul's
f: Steve's logic: "No one's expecting to see a homeless person as they're trying to find their way around that. Imagine the cash you'd make during the summer."
ex: Why not go to St. John's Wood or-
Yeah, I'd hang around in, maybe, say, the maze in Hampton Court.
No one's expecting to see a homeless person as they're trying to find their way around that. Imagine the cash you'd make during the summer.

q: At the wedding, the screeching girl's dad came over to Steve's DJ console. What did he do?
a: Joined in and sat her on his lap
x: Asked Steve to turn it down
f: Steve thought "He's gonna put paid to this", but "He comes over there, joins in." Ricky: "No!"
ex: So I'm thinking alright, her dad's coming over. He's gonna put paid to this. He's realized that, you know, she's causing a disturbance. He comes over there, joins in.
Sits her on his lap, he should say, "hey" - she's having a whale of a time. I'm thinking, I'm furious. I'm thinking, it's his responsibility to shut her up.
He's not going to do anything but what can I do? I can't step in.

q: In a panic at the wedding, Steve played a big floor-filler way too early and called it heresy. What was it?
f: Steve: "Loveshack's coming on way too soon... Oh, Loveshack before 11?" Then: "It's heresy, but I had to do it!"
ex: But, uh, but it just went- it really went from bad from worse and, and- you know there's that thing when you panic, you start panicking, so you start- you're putting on a lot of flavours that you would have saved to the- the, the last hour.
What we talking, 'Boom Boom Shake Shake the Room'?
You're throwing- exactly you're throwing them in early, Loveshack's coming on way too soon.
It's heresy, but I had to do it! But anyway, in the end, I made the bride go and get some people in. I thought- I said "Look, it's your special night, alright, and they're gonna enjoy this."

q: Ricky said Karl's head sometimes looks like a Halloween pumpkin. What did Steve say a Jack-o'-lantern has that Karl hasn't?
a: A certain light behind the eyes
x: A bit of colour in its cheeks
f: Steve: "When a Jack-o-Lantern sits outside someone's house right? There is a certain light behind the eyes." Then: "Not with Karl."
ex: Yeah, I love it. I just, I can't get enough of him. Because I see different things. Every time I look at Karl, sometimes I see like a completely sort of like spherical object, right? Like honestly, like some sort of pumpkin on you know...…
With a pumpkin, Rick... When a Jack-o-Lantern sits outside someone's house right? There is a certain light behind the eyes.

a: You drink the snake's still-beating heart from a glass

You have to name the snake before it's cooked
You get to keep the snake's fangs
f: Steve didn't go himself: "I didn't go because I was just a bit too squeamish." Ricky's review: "That's disgusting."
ex: So, I am quite exotic. I don't mind. I tell you what I didn't do though, I think I would be fascinated to have seen you down there. There's a place in Vietnam, just outside of Hanoi called Snake Village, right? And it is a long, long…

I mean, proper great, big mammoth snakes, sometimes even king cobras, which I think may even be endangered in some parts of the world. And anyway in snake Village you go over there. I didn't go because I was just a bit too squeamish, you…
The blood dribbles into a cup. And then, if you're the guest of honour, they take the still-beating heart and they make you drink it from a glass.

q: Steve mocked the NME, saying its letters page was full of people complaining about what?
a: The haircut of the bloke from the Kaiser Chiefs
x: The free CD on the front cover
f: Steve: "It's not a pressing concern. Move on." He also reckoned you can keep reading Rolling Stone "after you're about 16 years of age."
ex: Well, yeah, but you can- you can carry on reading Rolling Stone magazine after you're about 16 years of age.
The letters pages... People complaining about the haircut of the bloke from the Kaiser Chiefs.
It's not a pressing concern. Move on.

q: Remembering 'No Petting' signs at swimming baths, what did Steve imagine was the real reason the rule was brought in?
a: A lifeguard saw his ex-girlfriend getting off with a bloke in the pool
x: A councillor was caught snogging in the deep end
People kept bringing their dogs in for a swim
Pensioners complained about teenagers in the jacuzzi
f: Steve's jealous lifeguard: "No petting, you can't, you're not allowed to kiss. Her. Or anyone, no, no-one."
ex: It’s like you’re not allowed to kiss in a swimming baths.

And I love the idea it’s probably some kind of lifeguard who’s sort of, maybe saw his ex-girlfriend getting off with some bloke in the water and thought “Oh, bloody hell! Right there’s no petting anymore in here!”
”No petting, you can’t, you’re not allowed to kiss. Her. Or anyone, no, no-one.”

q: After the Alfred story, Ricky said Karl had 'the best mind working on radio today'. Who did Steve say was the only person who makes less sense?
f: Steve on Wogan: "I don't know what he's talking about... It's like free form poetry."
ex: Think of that. And so he then, I love the fact he hands out the guns and they do a deal, it’s just, honestly. You got the best, you’ve got the best mind working on radio today. It’s incredible.
See, the only person who makes less sense is Terry Wogan.
Ahhh…he goes up and down don’t he?
I don’t know what he’s talking about.
I can’t understand his sentences ‘cos I don’t know…

q: Mocking the 'treat others how you'd want to be treated' rule, what did Steve say he would want someone to do to him?
f: Ricky went first: he'd want someone to throw cake at him, "Because I'm a greedy bastard."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Society · 2009
ex: Also, this thing that every individual can go, "How would I want to be treated? Um, well, I'd want someone to throw cake at me."
I would want someone to steal my telly.

q: Karl admitted he thought Steve looked weird when they first met. What did he say had improved about Steve since then?
a: His hair's a bit smarter and he's got nicer glasses
f: Karl then undid the compliment: "Or I might have just got used to it."
ex: Yeah, you get used to it, and y- you have changed a little bit, your hair's a bit smarter now and you got some nicer glasses and that, I think.
Or I might have just got used to it.

q: Steve said nobody stopped his rival's illegal high jump because the games teachers were having a quick fag. What did he say one of them was called?
f: Ricky set it up ("What was his name again?... The fag.") and Steve finished it off: "I think his name was Mr Woodbine."
ex: Just the Games teachers having a quick fag.
Yeah, yeah. What was his name again?
I think his name was Mr Woodbine.

q: How did Steve plan to win Dido over without having to meet her in the flesh?
a: Send her a video of himself looking good on TV
x: Get Zane Lowe to put a word in
Turn up at her gig with flowers
f: Ricky's version: "This is me on Top TV Bastards, what do you think?... I'm certainly no worse, without the lighting and make-up."
ex: ...I'd wear a, actually what I'd do is go 'right, I'm not gonna meet you in the flesh, I'm gonna send a picture of me on video...'
“This is me on Top TV Bastards, what do you think?”
“And if you think it's good, well I'm certainly no worse, without the lighting and make-up, so don't worry about that.”

q: Steve said it was time for the Scottish Widow to move on from her late husband. How long did he say she'd been grieving?
f: Steve's message to her: "It's time to move on. He wouldn't want to see you like this."
ex: He worked hard on his lan--
"It's time to move on. He wouldn't want to see you like this--"

q: After vowing to do a brilliant 50 minutes without Karl, the studio went silent. How did Steve nervously try to fill it?
a: He started a story about growing up in Manchester
x: He started reading the travel news
He started reading out the weather
f: Steve, borrowing Karl's life: "I remember when I was growing up in Manchester--" Ricky: "No, you can't..."
ex: (Nervously) Aww, (Exhales) is it- I was just--
You were just gonna say sommat.
(laughing slightly) Yeah. Yeah. No, I- I remember when I was... I remember when I was growing up in Manchester--

q: Steve moaned that a magazine mocked him for shopping in charity shops, when he's giving money to charity. What did he admit was really the point?
f: The magazine marvelled that despite all his money "he's still going in charity shops". Ricky: "To save 50p?" Steve: "To save 50p of course!"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Comic Relief · 2011
ex: Ever since I was young, I've always liked going in charity shops, particularly because you find sort of interesting old records in there. Never sort of gone in there to buy clothes and stuff, but books, whatever. And I was in a charity…
I'm giving my money to a charity. Isn't that a noble cause? I mean, obviously that's not the reason I'm doing it. I'm doing it...

q: Steve hoped his charity-shop purchases would slowly accumulate towards what?
f: Ricky: "I think you got to do a bit more than get Roger Whittaker's greatest hits for 10p."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Comic Relief · 2011
ex: Occasionally I'll shoplift! I'm no mug. 70p?! Don't you think that seems frustrating, though, that?
Yeah, but what do you expect? What are they going to do? They're not going to say, Steve Merchant, heart of gold are they?
I just thought all these things would slowly accumulate towards the OBE.
Yeah, I know. I think you got to do a bit more than get Roger Whittaker's greatest hits for 10p.

q: Steve's old trick for dodging people in the street was pretending to be vaguely foreign. What did he do when a charity collector asked "Are you Stephen Merchant?"
a: Kept up the act and said he didn't know who that was
x: Admitted it and signed up on the spot
Signed an autograph and legged it
f: He chose to carry on the lie: "I don't know who that is." The collector: "Really? You look a lot like him."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Comic Relief · 2011
ex: And the guy said, are you Stephen Merchant?
No. Sorry! Not when you were famous?!
Because it hadn't occurred to me. It was like a lapse of concentration.
It was a lapse of concentration because.

q: Steve was outraged that Habitat wanted two quid for its catalogue. What did he say would have made him happy to pay?
a: Ladies draped over the filing cabinets
x: A free cushion with every copy
